You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Beneficial Bancorp, Inc. realized record after merger with WSFS Financial Corporation, ~2021-2023 horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because Beneficial Bancorp, Inc. was absorbed
> into the surviving corporation and deregistered, there is no post-closing public
> financial-reporting record for Beneficial as a standalone entity; this sub-dossier
> traces the surviving registrant's later public filings to establish what, if
> anything, is separately observable. It contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Closing and deregistration (feasibility-relevant)
- The merger of Beneficial Bancorp, Inc. into WSFS Financial Corporation (with the
  simultaneous merger of Beneficial Bank into WSFS Bank) was completed on March 1,
  2019. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-19-011959, 8-K Item 2.01]
- Upon completion, Beneficial's common stock was withdrawn from quotation on the Nasdaq
  Global Select Market as of close of business February 28, 2019, and price quotations
  for Beneficial common stock ceased to be available in the public market. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-19-011959, 8-K Item 3.01]
- On March 11, 2019, a Form 15 was filed on behalf of Beneficial Bancorp, Inc.
  (executed by WSFS Financial Corporation "as successor to Beneficial Bancorp, Inc."),
  certifying termination of registration of Beneficial's common stock under Section
  12(g)/12(h) of the Exchange Act, with the approximate number of holders of record
  listed as "None." [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-19-013839, Form 15-12B]
- No further periodic reports (10-K, 10-Q) were filed under Beneficial Bancorp, Inc.'s
  own SEC registrant record (CIK 0001615418) after its final FY2018 Form 10-K filed
  February 26, 2019; the entity's EDGAR filing history ends with the March 2019
  deregistration filings. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-19-013839, Form 15-12B]

## Surviving registrant's subsequent public disclosure of the acquired business
- WSFS Financial Corporation (CIK 0000828944), the surviving corporation, continued to
  file its own periodic reports after the merger, including Form 10-K for fiscal year
  2021 (filed 2022) and fiscal year 2022 (filed 2023). [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]
- In both the FY2021 and FY2022 Form 10-K, WSFS discloses only two reportable operating
  segments for goodwill-impairment and segment-reporting purposes — "WSFS Bank" and
  "Wealth Management" — with goodwill presented on a consolidated/segment basis; neither
  filing presents a separate reporting line, segment, or disclosed financial result
  specifically isolating the former Beneficial Bank franchise. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]
- In both years, WSFS states that, based on its qualitative assessment, no goodwill
  impairment existed for the year then ended (December 31, 2021; December 31, 2022),
  reported for the consolidated "WSFS Bank" and "Wealth Management" reporting units as a
  whole rather than for Beneficial specifically. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]
- The only remaining references to "Beneficial Bank" by name in the FY2021 and FY2022
  Form 10-K are administrative/legacy items — a Beneficial Bank other-postretirement
  benefit plan discount-rate disclosure and exhibit-index references to legacy
  Beneficial Bank compensation-plan documents (e.g., a Supplemental Pension and
  Retirement Plan, a Stock-Based Deferral Plan, and an Elective Deferred Compensation
  Plan) originally filed in 2019 — not a disclosed post-close operating or financial
  trajectory for the acquired franchise. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- No reputable-press or SEC-filed disclosure specifically isolating the realized
  performance, integration outcome, or disruption record of the former Beneficial
  Bank franchise within WSFS for the 2021-2023 window was located; any such
  business-level narrative for this window is [UNVERIFIED].

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Beneficial Bancorp, Inc. deregistered from SEC reporting effective March 2019
  following its whole-company merger into WSFS Financial Corporation, and has filed no
  periodic reports since. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-19-013839, Form 15-12B]
- The surviving registrant, WSFS Financial Corporation, continued to report
  consolidated results across two operating segments ("WSFS Bank" and "Wealth
  Management") through fiscal years 2021 and 2022, with no goodwill impairment recorded
  in either year at the consolidated/segment level, but at no point in the reviewed
  filings does WSFS separately disclose a financial or operating trajectory specific to
  the acquired Beneficial franchise. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]
- Because no public source separately discloses the acquired business's post-close
  trajectory, the realized 3-5-year outcome for this case is UNCERTAIN (no public
  record) rather than inferable from WSFS's consolidated results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-22-004404, 10-K FY2021] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-23-005573, 10-K FY2022]

[SLICE END]
